A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Speculative Jacobi Decoding (SJD) work. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-generation experiments, FID and CLIP scores, acceleration measurements, and ablations in Section 5 and Appendices B–E.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds Anole comparisons, quality and token-probability measurements, a refinement ablation, and diversity and failure analyses.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the same acceptance rule, rejection resampling, remaining-token sampling, sliding window, and spatial initialization strategies. The refinement examined in new Appendix F is the existing Equation (3), not a newly introduced method component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate text-to-image generation using MSCOCO2017 and Parti-prompts. LlamaGen evaluations and qualitative Emu3 examples already appear in v1. The additional prompts and failure examples remain within the existing image-generation coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 4–5 add Jacobi decoding and SJD without spatial initialization to Anole comparisons that previously contained only original decoding and SJD with spatial initialization. Tables 7–8 also include original autoregression in the corresponding sampling and resolution analyses. These extend existing comparison families.

E3.justification: v2 substantially extends evaluation through HPSv2, perplexity, token-probability measurements, and controls that replace unaccepted tokens instead of refining them. These are added evaluation procedures; the previously reported benchmark splits, default model and sampling settings, and parameter sweeps are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds quality measurements to the previously speed-focused ablations (Tables 7–10), perplexity and token-probability checks (Tables 6 and 11), and a refinement-disabled control (Appendix F, Figure 14). New diversity and artifact analyses in Appendices G–H substantially broaden investigation of mechanisms and limitations.

E5.justification: v2 clarifies shared seeds in Figure 2 and specifies seed matching in Figure 17. Table 11 newly reports across-token standard deviations, which describe token variability rather than run-to-run uncertainty. The ten-seed initialization study remains unchanged, and no increase in repeated runs is stated.

E6.justification: Pre-existing scores and acceleration ratios in Tables 1–3 are retained. v2 adds absolute timings, Anole comparison rows, quality and probability statistics, and qualitative findings. For example, Table 4 newly reports Anole with Jacobi decoding at 1.03× latency acceleration and FID 29.34; Figure 14 adds substantial step-count differences between refinement controls.

T1.justification: Theorem 1, its conditional-independence assumption, and proof Equations (4)–(13) are unchanged. Figure 4 corrects a conditioning index to match the already-existing Equation (3), without revising the mathematical argument.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central claims: training-free probabilistic Jacobi decoding, no auxiliary draft model, approximately 2× acceleration with little quality loss, and spatial initialization benefits in suitable scenarios. Rewording the contribution statement does not change its scientific scope.

C2.justification: v2 attributes acceleration specifically to repeated refinement of unaccepted tokens, interprets probability statistics and sampling-driven diversity, and discusses why identical seeds need not produce identical images. Appendix H newly acknowledges acceptance of artifact-bearing token sequences in complex images. These substantially extend v1's mechanism discussion and applicability limits.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-access link and identifies A100 and RTX4090 hardware for Tables 1–2. These are additional disclosures, not evidence that existing experiments changed hardware; Appendix C already documented its timing setup in v1. Appendix D also drops the explicit 3.1B LlamaGen parameter-count comparison.

R1.justification: Section 2 more precisely distinguishes CLLM's fine-tuning and Lookahead Decoding's n-gram pool from SJD. Added citations support fixed-point refinement, HPSv2, perplexity discussion, and autoregressive video generation. The overall positioning relative to Jacobi and speculative decoding remains intact.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most prose are retained, with localized revisions to the introduction, related work, and conclusion. v2 adds acknowledgments, a conference header, and appendix subsections; existing limitations and broader impacts move from F–G to I–J.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 4–11 and Figures 14–18, expands Tables 1–2 with absolute-latency columns, and redraws Figure 4 to clarify probability vectors and the Jacobi window. Figure 2's seed caption is revised. Existing Lumina-mGPT and Emu3 galleries are retained but exchanged in order and numbering.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens evaluation of the central acceleration–quality tradeoff. v1's speed-focused ablations gain CLIP and HPSv2 checks, the refinement-disabled control tests the proposed mechanism, and explicit failure examples expose practical limits. More complete Anole comparisons and absolute timings further improve assessability. These gains address important evidential gaps, although failure frequency and run-to-run uncertainty remain unquantified.
